transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-08-18
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Lucia Chen (Redwood SE), Jordan Park (Redwood SE), Maya Ortiz (Hyperion CTO), Ethan Cole (Hyperion ML Eng), Priya Singh (Infra), Noah Gray (Data Scientist)
Recording link: (fireflies)

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — I'm Samir, AE on the account, lucia and jordan are our SEs. Maya, Ethan, priya, thanks for making time. int'l timezone apologies.
[00:15] Maya: Hi, thanks. we wanted to focus this session on quantization impacts — both accuracy and perf — for our on-prem cluster.
[00:30] Lucia: Great. quick agenda: we walk quantization options (INT8/FP8/GPTQ/AWQ), show perf vs latency tradeoffs, discuss KV cache/batching interactions, and then plan a pilot. does that align?
[00:45] Maya: Yes. main goal: move a 13B model to our private infra with acceptable latency (<=120ms p95) and <5% accuracy drop on our eval set.
[01:05] Ethan: Also concerned about tail latency when prefix cache misses happen — we do lots of few-shot prompts with long prefixes.
[01:20] Jordan: Perfect — we'll cover caching strategies. quick note: quantization can change kernel selection at runtime; that affects latency unpredictability.
[01:40] Priya: On infra: we're on bare-metal A100s (80GB) but have older T4 fleet for burst. interested in how INT8/FP8 maps to those cards.
[01:55] Lucia: Right — FP8 typically requires newer compilers / runtime support; on A100 we're good, T4s don't support FP8 well. INT8/GPTQ/AWQ are more portable.
[02:10] Samir: quick level-set on terms: when we say GPTQ, we mean post-training quant using per-channel scales and block-wise quant; AWQ is the more recent algorithm with adaptive weight quantization. customers often see AWQ slightly better accuracy than naive GPTQ on some models.
[02:30] Maya: we've seen notes online but worried about regression on our entity-extraction tasks. small changes blow up F1.
[02:45] Lucia: totally. that's why calibration sets + eval harness matter. We'll run both intrinsic metrics (perplexity) and your task metrics (F1/EM) side-by-side.
[03:00] Noah: do you have a recommended calibration size? we have ~10k labeled examples but could subset.
[03:15] Jordan: usually 1-2k representative examples gives stable scales for GPTQ/AWQ; for AWQ sometimes 500 carefully chosen prompts is enough but better to include diverse lengths.
[03:35] Ethan: What about FP8 — is it less likely to regress?
[03:50] Lucia: FP8 can preserve more dynamic range for activations vs INT8 weight-only quant, so sometimes better. but FP8 adoption requires end-to-end support: model compiler, runtimes that can do FP8 GEMMs, and possibly kernel fusions. on A100 we can get FP8 benefits, but still watch for alignment on layernorm/softmax ops — small numeric changes can shift outputs.
[04:15] Maya: latency numbers — do you have ballpark throughput for 13B using INT8 vs FP8?
[04:30] Jordan: ballpark: on a80-ish hw with optimized kernels, INT8 can give 2.2-2.6x speedup vs FP16 for generation; FP8 often sits at ~1.8-2.2x depending on kernels. but depends on sequence length, KV cache hit rates, and batch size.
[04:55] Priya: sequence len for us is typically 512 tokens, but many requests are short (30-120) with long prefixes cached.
[05:10] Lucia: caching is key — if prefix KV cache is warm, per-step latency drops a lot. however, quantized models may have different memory layout and affect KV cache prefetching. we've seen small cases where quantized model increases first-token latency due to different memory copies.
[05:35] Ethan: We've been hitting p95 spikes when a cached session gets evicted and rewarm takes 2-3 seconds. can quantization reduce memory footprint enough to keep more cache resident?
[05:50] Jordan: yes, INT8/AWQ typically reduce model size by ~2-4x; that can let you keep more sessions hot. but watch tradeoff: if quantization causes slower per-op kernels due to lack of fused kernels, you might not get net latency wins on first token.
[06:15] Maya: Any specific models you've seen problematic with GPTQ/AWQ?
[06:30] Lucia: Layer normalization sensitivity is a recurring pain point. LLaMA-family forks sometimes need per-layer tweaks. Also instruction-tuned finetunes can amplify small numeric shifts, so you may need to run a small fine-tune or bias correction pass.
[06:55] Priya: On the ops side — VPC/on-prem: we need to ensure KMS integration for keys and audit logs. How does your private deployment support that?
[07:10] Samir: Redwood Private offers KMS/HSM integrations and audit logging; we can run in your VPC and integrate to your KMS provider. Lucia can attach the security doc.
[07:25] Lucia: Yes, we'll send the SOC2/ISO excerpts and the private deploy runbook after the call. a note: for on-prem we can bundle pre-quantized artifacts, or build quantization in-cluster — both are possible. bundling pre-quantized images simplifies runtime.
[07:45] Ethan: If we bundle pre-quantized images, whats the workflow for A/B comparing baseline vs quantized?
[08:00] Jordan: we typically provide side-by-side endpoints and run canary traffic; also provide a deterministic eval harness so you can reproduce diffs. we recommend exporting logits for a probe set to compare distribution shifts.
[08:20] Noah: about regressions: what magnitude of F1 drop have you seen and when it's unacceptable?
[08:35] Lucia: varies. INT8/GPTQ sometimes shows <1-3% relative drop on robust models, but for fragile tasks it can be 5-10% unless you do per-layer tweaks or light fine-tune. AWQ often reduces that delta, but not guaranteed.
[08:55] Maya: Are there mitigation strategies besides fine-tune?
[09:10] Lucia: Yes: mixed precision (keep sensitive layers in FP16 or FP32), per-channel bias correction, activation range clipping, and revisiting tokenization / prompt formatting. Also ensemble outputs between FP16 and quantized for critical requests (costly but works).
[09:30] Ethan: cost / throughput — any guidance on batch sizes? we want low latency but also need decent throughput for nightly jobs.
[09:45] Jordan: For online low-latency APIs, batch sizes of 1-8 are common; larger batches favor throughput but increase tail. Quantized models may allow slightly larger batches before GPU memory becomes a constraint. For offline jobs, batch sizes 32+ yield best token/s.
[10:10] Priya: kernel selection & runtime: will Redwood runtime pick best kernel automatically across quantized variants?
[10:25] Lucia: Yes, runtime has kernel selector heuristics based on model shape, seq len, and hardware; for quantized models we add heuristics for fused int8 GEMMs vs fallback FP16. there can be corner cases where manual override helps.
[10:45] Maya: do you have any public benchmark spreadsheets we can look at? we want realistic baselines.
[11:00] Samir: we'll share the spreadsheet. Jordan is prepping the skeleton. It will include p50/p95 latencies, tokens/s, and F1/per-task metrics for baseline and quantized runs.
[11:15] Ethan: On GPTQ vs AWQ — which toolchain do you recommend if we want reproducible pipelines?
[11:30] Jordan: AWQ has been more robust lately for certain LLMs; GPTQ is mature and well-understood. Our suggestion: try both on your calibration set and measure. AWQ sometimes needs specific compilers/ops. we'll automate both in the bench.
[11:50] Lucia: also watch out for tokenizer differences — if a quantization process changes tokenization caching behavior it can look like a model regression but is actually preproc mismatch.
[12:05] Noah: anything about FP8 vs INT8 for memory-bound workloads?
[12:20] Jordan: FP8 helps with dynamic range and can improve activation compute speed if kernels are available, but it's less common on older hardware. INT8 has broad support and often still the best cost/benefit on heterogeneous fleets.
[12:40] Maya: what about fallback when a quantized model fails a threshold? can Redwood runtime automatically route to a higher-precision variant?
[12:55] Samir: yes — we support smart routing and automatic fallback to FP16/FP32 variants based on policy (latency, quality thresholds, error rates). you can set thresholds per-route.
[13:10] Priya: On monitoring — do you capture token-level cost and accuracy drift?
[13:25] Lucia: we record per-request latencies, token counts, error rates, and can hook custom evals to detect quality regressions tied to prompt buckets. we can set alerts for degradation beyond configurable thresholds.
[13:45] Maya: ok practical ask: we'd like a short pilot — run three models (13B instruction-tuned baseline, 13B + GPTQ, 13B + AWQ) on our calibration set and give p50/p95 and F1 changes.
[14:05] Samir: agreeable. timeline? two weeks doable if we get data access and infra creds.
[14:20] Ethan: we can provide the dataset by Friday (2026-08-21).
[14:35] Samir: great. lucia/jordan will run bench and upload. we'll also include notes on mixed-precision fallbacks.
[14:50] Maya: any gotchas we should prepare for on our KMS / VPC side?
[15:05] Lucia: ensure outbound access for the installer if you want Redwood to orchestrate builds; otherwise we can do an air-gapped bundle. KMS key policies should allow signing/unwrap for inference nodes. we'll send exact ports and policies.
[15:25] Priya: ok. last question: any known models where AWQ causes unexpected hallucination shifts?
[15:40] Jordan: not broadly, but instruction-tuned small-changes amplify hallucinations sometimes; that's where the evaluation harness and rollback policy helps.
[15:55] Samir: wrapping up — recap next steps and owners.
[16:05] Maya: thanks, this was helpful.
[16:10] Samir: we'll send the docs and bench plan after the call. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
